incidents.title: System.Messaging (MSMQ) is not supported on .NET Core / .NET 5+
incidents.description: The application uses System.Messaging for MSMQ-based notification queuing. System.Messaging is a Windows-only, .NET Framework library that is not available in .NET Core or .NET 5+.
incidents.recommendation: Replace MSMQ with a cloud-native messaging service such as Azure Service Bus, Azure Queue Storage, or RabbitMQ via the MassTransit or NServiceBus abstraction libraries.

incidents.title: System.Web.* namespace is not available in .NET Core / .NET 5+
incidents.description: The project heavily depends on System.Web.Mvc, System.Web.Optimization, System.Web.Routing and other System.Web types which do not exist in .NET Core.
incidents.recommendation: Migrate to ASP.NET Core MVC. Replace System.Web.Mvc.Controller with Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Controller, update routing to attribute-based or endpoint routing, replace BundleConfig with Bundler & Minifier or Webpack.

incidents.title: ConfigurationManager is not the recommended configuration approach in .NET Core
incidents.description: System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager is used to read connection strings and app settings from Web.config. In .NET Core, Web.config is not the primary configuration mechanism.
incidents.recommendation: Replace ConfigurationManager with Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration (IConfiguration) and use appsettings.json. Inject IConfiguration via dependency injection.

incidents.title: Global.asax / HttpApplication startup pattern not supported in .NET Core
incidents.description: The application relies on Global.asax and HttpApplication lifecycle for application startup and initialization. .NET Core uses the Program.cs / Startup.cs (or top-level statements) model.
incidents.recommendation: Migrate startup code to Program.cs using the WebApplication builder pattern. Move database initialization to IHostedService or application startup.

incidents.title: Entity Framework Core 3.1 is end-of-life; upgrade to EF Core 8+
incidents.description: The project uses EF Core 3.1.32 which reached end-of-life in December 2022. This version does not receive security patches.
incidents.recommendation: Upgrade to EF Core 8.x (for .NET 8) or EF Core 9.x (for .NET 9+). Review breaking changes in the EF Core migration guide.

incidents.title: Web.config should be replaced with appsettings.json
incidents.description: Connection strings and application settings stored in Web.config are .NET Framework / IIS specific. Modern .NET applications use appsettings.json with optional environment-specific overrides.
incidents.recommendation: Migrate connection strings and appSettings keys to appsettings.json. Use environment variables or Azure App Configuration for environment-specific settings.

incidents.title: Manual dependency instantiation; no dependency injection container
incidents.description: The application manually instantiates SchoolContext and NotificationService in BaseController constructors rather than using a DI container.
incidents.recommendation: Register services in Program.cs using builder.Services. Inject IDbContextFactory<SchoolContext> or SchoolContext directly through controller constructors. Register NotificationService as a scoped or singleton service.
incidents.apiChange: Manual new() instantiation -> IServiceProvider / constructor injection

incidents.title: SQL Server LocalDB used for development - should use a configurable connection
incidents.description: The connection string points to SQL Server LocalDB which is a developer tool and not suitable for cloud or container deployments.
incidents.recommendation: Use environment variables or Key Vault references for database connection strings. For cloud deployment target Azure SQL Database or Azure SQL Managed Instance.
incidents.apiChange: LocalDB connection string -> Environment variable / Azure Key Vault reference

incidents.title: CSRF protection uses legacy AntiForgeryToken pattern
incidents.description: The application uses Html.AntiForgeryToken() and [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] which are ASP.NET MVC 5 patterns. ASP.NET Core MVC uses IAntiforgery service and [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken].
incidents.recommendation: After migration to ASP.NET Core, use the built-in antiforgery service. Consider using [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] at the application level.

incidents.title: File upload uses HttpPostedFileBase which is not available in .NET Core
incidents.description: The CoursesController uses HttpPostedFileBase for file uploads, which is a System.Web type.
incidents.recommendation: Replace HttpPostedFileBase with IFormFile from Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.

incidents.title: packages.config NuGet format must be migrated to PackageReference
incidents.description: The project uses the legacy packages.config NuGet package management format. Modern .NET SDK-style projects use PackageReference in .csproj.
incidents.recommendation: Migrate from packages.config to PackageReference format using Visual Studio or the nuget migrate command. This is required before migrating to SDK-style project format.

incidents.title: Non-SDK project format (.csproj) must be converted to SDK-style
incidents.description: The project uses the old .NET Framework MSBuild project format which is not compatible with .NET 5+ SDK-style projects.
incidents.recommendation: Convert to SDK-style project format by rewriting the .csproj file with <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">. Use the Upgrade Assistant tool for automated conversion.

incidents.title: Newtonsoft.Json should be replaced with System.Text.Json for new .NET targets
incidents.description: The project uses Newtonsoft.Json 13.x. While this library still works in .NET Core, the built-in System.Text.Json is generally preferred for new development in .NET 5+.
incidents.recommendation: Consider replacing Newtonsoft.Json with System.Text.Json where possible, particularly for simple serialization scenarios. Retain Newtonsoft.Json where complex serialization is needed.

incidents.title: Razor views (.cshtml) need minor syntax updates for ASP.NET Core
incidents.description: Existing CSHTML views use ASP.NET MVC 5 HTML helpers (Html.BeginForm, Html.TextBoxFor, etc.). ASP.NET Core Razor uses Tag Helpers as the preferred approach.
incidents.recommendation: Consider migrating HTML helpers to Tag Helpers (asp-action, asp-controller, asp-for attributes) for better readability. HTML helpers still work in ASP.NET Core.

incidents.title: Logging uses System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine instead of ILogger
incidents.description: The application uses System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine and a custom LoggingService instead of the .NET standard ILogger<T> abstraction.
incidents.recommendation: Replace with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger<T>. This provides structured logging, multiple sinks (console, Application Insights, etc.), and configuration-based log levels.

incidents.title: No authentication or authorization implemented
incidents.description: The application has no authentication or authorization. Controllers and actions are all publicly accessible.
incidents.recommendation: For production cloud deployment, add ASP.NET Core Identity, Azure AD / Entra ID authentication, or another identity provider. Use [Authorize] attributes to protect sensitive operations.

incidents.title: File uploads stored on local filesystem; not suitable for cloud scale-out
incidents.description: The CoursesController saves uploaded files to the server local filesystem (~/Uploads). This pattern does not work in horizontally scaled or ephemeral cloud environments.
incidents.recommendation: Store uploaded files in Azure Blob Storage or another cloud object store. Use the Azure.Storage.Blobs SDK and return a URL/reference rather than a file path.

incidents.title: Table-per-Hierarchy (TPH) inheritance for Person entity needs verification with newer EF Core
incidents.description: The SchoolContext configures TPH inheritance for the Person entity (Student/Instructor). EF Core 7+ changed how TPH discriminators work by default.
incidents.recommendation: After upgrading to EF Core 7+, verify TPH behavior still works as expected. Consider explicit discriminator column type configuration.
incidents.apiChange: EF Core 3.1 TPH -> EF Core 7+ TPH (verify discriminator configuration)
